finalText:
Rule written: `/private/var/folders/11/m_kwnqr97632l_cjt0mhytvh0000gn/T/pstack-live-UJlC0V/agent/pstack/pstack-models.mdc` (`alwaysApply: true`, budget `large (xhigh)`). It applies to new sessions; re-running `/setup-pstack` rewrites it.

**What happened to the mapping.** I detected these families for `Task`: `openai` (gpt-4…gpt-6.1-sol, o-series), `zai` (glm-4.7…glm-5.3-highspeed), `deepseek` (deepseek-flash, deepseek-v4-pro). The skill defaults are all `claude-opus-5-5-*` and `grok-4.7-*`, and neither the Claude nor the Grok family is available here — so "closest same-family model, else `inherit-parent`" resolves to `inherit-parent` for every role. `inherit-parent` always passes validation, and the `large` budget is a no-op on aliases.

Two consequences worth knowing:

- Every pstack role now runs on the parent chat model. That's the same behavior as having no rule, so this file currently pins nothing except the budget declaration and the fan-out shape.
- Panel lists (`arena runners`, `arena cross-judge pool`, `architect runners`, `interrogate reviewers`) kept **two** entries so the fan-out count is unchanged, even though both entries are now the same alias — those pairs run as two same-model subagents.

If you'd rather have real slugs pinned, the available set above means pstack roles would have to move to `openai/gpt-5.6-sol`-class or `zai/glm-5.3`-class models. Say the word and I'll map each role onto those families instead.

Skipped in Pi: steps 7 and 8 offers (verify skill / formal verification skill) — you said not to ask; the workspace is an empty git checkout with no `verify-*` or formal-verification skill, so either could be generated later with `/create-verification-skill` or `/create-formal-verification-skill`.

For a parent chat to loop on: nothing blocking here.
